title: Reinhart et al., Do LLMs write like humans? (PNAS 2025;122:e2422455122)
effect: GPT-4o 5.3x human rate (d=1.38); instruction-tuned models 2-5x. Differences larger for instruction-tuned than base models and persist in larger models.
models: GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, Llama 3 8B/70B base and Instruct
fix: Finish the sentence; make the participial tail its own sentence with a real subject, or cut it.

title: Reinhart et al. (nominalizations)
fix: Turn the noun back into a verb with a person as subject ('the implementation of X' becomes 'they built X').

title: Reinhart et al. (other grammar)
feature: Subject 'that' clauses; phrasal coordination; agentless passive; downtoners; clausal coordination
effect: 'that' subject clauses 2.6x (d=0.77); phrasal coordination 1.9x (d=0.81); agentless passive about half human rate (GPT-4o); downtoners (barely, nearly) up in GPT-4o, down in Llama 3; clausal coordination avoided by GPT-4o, overused by Llama 3. Models differ from each other, so there is no single LLM grammar.
fix: Humans use more agentless passives and more clause-joining; fewer passives is not automatically more human.

title: Reinhart et al. Table 1 (word ratios vs human, fiction-style prompts)
effect: GPT-4o: camaraderie 162x, tapestry 155x, intricate 119x, underscore 107x, amidst 100x, palpable 95x, solace 95x. Llama 3 70B Instruct: unease 63x, palpable 47x, camaraderie 24x. Llama 3 8B Instruct: unease 101x, palpable 48x.
fix: Name the specific feeling or object; these abstract mood words stand in for detail.

title: Liang et al., Monitoring AI-Modified Content at Scale
feature: Share of LLM-modified text in peer reviews
effect: 6.5% to 16.9% of reviews at ICLR 2024, NeurIPS 2023, CoRL 2023, EMNLP 2023 substantially LLM-modified. Word list not read (abstract page only).

title: Paech et al., Antislop (ICLR 2026)
feature: Fiction slop = words, names, n-grams over-represented vs human baseline (wordfreq; Reddit creative writing + Gutenberg for n-grams)
effect: gemma-3-12b: 'elara' 85,513x, 'unsettlingly' 3,833x, 'shimmered' 2,882x, 'stammered' 2,043x; trigrams 'heart hammered ribs' 1,192x, 'voice trembling slightly' 731x, 'felt profound sense' 550x. Across 67 models, 'flickered' in the top list for 98.5%, 'voice barely whisper' trigram for 68.7%. Fingerprints cluster by model family. Categories: recurring names (Elara, Kael), sensory cliches, intensifiers, 'It's not X, it's Y'.
models: Gemma-3-12B main; Mistral-Small-3.2, Llama-3.3-70B similar; 67 models for cross-model counts
fix: Replace stock beats and names with scene-specific detail and names from outside the model; a banned-phrase list works for sampling but a writer must supply the specific thing.

title: Paech et al., Antislop ('not X, but Y')
feature: 'It's not X, it's Y' / 'not X, but Y' contrast
effect: 6.3x human prevalence in some models; a regex ban cut it to 0.00 hits per 1k chars on qwen3-4b.
models: some models (unspecified here); qwen3-4b for the ban test

title: Padmakumar & He, Does Writing with LMs Reduce Content Diversity? (ICLR 2024)
effect: Rouge-L similarity of key points: solo 0.1536, GPT3 0.1578 (ns), InstructGPT 0.1660 (p<0.05). Unique 5-grams: solo 0.991, GPT3 0.988, InstructGPT 0.977. Unique key points down similarly. The sameness came from the model's text; users' own text was unchanged. Models supplied about a third of characters. Feedback-tuned model only; base model did not homogenise.
fix: Write the key points yourself; use the model for phrasing at most. Tuned models narrow, not base ones.

title: The Last Fingerprint: How Markdown Training Shapes LLM Prose
feature: Em dash per 1,000 words; link to markdown habit
effect: Unconstrained 1000-word essays, ten topics: GPT-4.1 10.62, Claude Opus 4.6 9.09, Claude Sonnet 4 8.29, Claude Haiku 3.5 7.51, DeepSeek V3 6.95, GPT-4o 4.12, Gemini 2.5 Pro 3.53, GPT-5.4 1.43, Llama 0.00. Human baseline 3.23 (8 essays, 57k words; range 0.33-17.12, so tiny and noisy). Told to write plain prose with no markdown: Opus 4.6 fell to 0.19, GPT-4.1 only to 9.10. Opus 4.6 with markdown suppressed plus 'no em dashes': 0.00. Claude em dashes track markdown suppression; GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek persist.
models: 12 models incl. Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4, Haiku 3.5
fix: Ask for flowing prose without markdown and the dash mostly goes for Claude; otherwise edit dashes to commas or periods.

title: Report on Graphite 'AI Tells' and Opus 5.5 update (secondary; primary data CC BY 4.0)
feature: Claude-specific tells per version, em dash drift, phrase multiples
effect: 10k pre-2022 Common Crawl articles vs 90k SEO-style AI articles, one fixed prompt (not chat). Em dash/1k words, human 3.14: Opus 4 0.66, 4.6 0.20, 5 2.92, 5.5 0.015; GPT-4.1 7.13, GPT-5 6.92. Same model shifts about 5x by task (Arena 15.2 to 0.8; Arize 12.9 to 0.05 for Opus 5 to 5.5). Opus 5.5 phrase multiples vs human: 'this matters' 116x, 'is more than a _ it' 98x, 'why _ matters' 92x, 'looking ahead the' 40x, 'rather than simply' 32x, 'adds another layer' 27x, 'dependable' 23x. Tells turn over between versions (consecutive versions share 18.7-45.5% of lists); suppressing one tell shifts others in. Mean strength of 11 known tells fell 53% from Opus 4 to 5.5.
models: Claude Opus 4, 4.6, 5, 5.5; GPT-4.1, 5, 5.6, 6; Gemini 2.5 Pro, 3.1 Pro
fix: Do not edit against a fixed list; the list moves per model version. Cut thesis-announcing phrases ('this matters', 'more than just') and state the consequence.

title: Bakhshi, Saying More Than They Know (epistemic-rhetorical miscalibration)
effect: Per search summary only, PDF unreadable here: LLM text 7.13 tricolons per document vs 3.73 for human experts, strongest differentiator (p<0.001). Corpus, models and document length not verified; treat as unconfirmed.
fix: Vary list length; use two items or one.

title: Voice Under Revision (LLM rewriting of personal narrative)
feature: Residual source-style signal after LLM rewrite
effect: Per search summary only: stylometric attribution back to source 14.3% for GPT-5.4 rewrites vs 1.7% Claude Sonnet and 1.0% Gemini 3.1 Pro (chance 0.3%). Claude and Gemini erase the original voice more. Not read in full.
fix: When revising with an LLM, expect your voice flattened; keep original sentences and edit by hand.
